subject: Consent pathway & output clauses review — StellarMed order form
messages:
From: Janet Liu <janet.liu@stellarmed.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: StellarMed Procurement <procurement@stellarmed.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify output ownership & training consent in order form

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the call this morning. We've reviewed the draft order form and our legal team has two items we need clarified before procurement can proceed:

1) Output ownership: Section 4.2 appears to grant Redwood broad use rights in service outputs. Our product team requires clear assignment/confirmation that StellarMed retains exclusive rights to customer-generated outputs (reports, labels, patient-facing content) produced by the service.

2) Training/Feedback license: The order form references a "feedback" license back to Redwood. We need to understand whether StellarMed data, or derived outputs, could be used to train Redwood models (or be included in any training corpus) — and whether opting out is available.

I attached the latest mark-up from our procurement counsel (StellarMed_OrderForm_v3.docx). Can you confirm Redwood's position and provide proposed contract language or redlines we can review? If helpful, our counsel (Tim O'Neill) is copied and available to discuss.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is targeting signing by end of month.

Best,
Janet Liu
Head of Contracts
StellarMed Inc
[Attachment: StellarMed_OrderForm_v3.docx]
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify output ownership & training consent in order form

Team — forwarding StellarMed's ask. Procurement wants explicit outcome on output ownership and a clear opt-out for training/feedback. Key constraints: we need feedback telemetry to diagnose regressions and for safety, but for enterprise deals we generally offer a training opt-out and carve an audit/telemetry exception (redwood anonymized telemetry for operational safety).

Proposed internal questions to resolve before we send wording:
- Do we want to offer wholesale assignment of output ownership (yes/no)? Implications for productization downstream.
- If we allow assignment/ownership to customer, can we reserve a perpetual, non-exclusive feedback license limited to improving service quality (no model retraining without explicit consent)?
- Can we define telemetry in the SOW as "operational telemetry and safety logs" excluded from the opt-out?

Connor — can you flag any infra/ops concerns about carving out telemetry?
Ben — legal: please draft two short options (A: customer-assignment + limited feedback license; B: customer-ownership + explicit training prohibition + paid training license if requested).
Grace — product: how would assignment impact our downstream guardrails for aggregated features and analytics?

Goal: reconcile internally today and send a one-page redline with suggested language to Janet by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Mina
Senior Sales Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Clarify output ownership & training consent in order form

Folks — drafting two short, customer-facing options below. I kept the language intentionally prescriptive to avoid back-and-forth. I'll attach a tracked redline in an hour (redlines_stellarmed.docx).

Option A (Recommended for enterprise):
- Customer ownership: "Customer shall own all right, title and interest in and to Outputs generated solely from Customer Content and prompts."
- Feedback license (narrow): "Customer grants Redwood a perpetual, royalty-free, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use Customer Feedback solely to improve the Redwood service, provided that such Feedback shall not be used to retrain or otherwise incorporate Customer Content or Outputs into Redwood's base or derivative training datasets without Customer's prior written consent."
- Telemetry carve: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may collect and retain operational telemetry and anonymized system logs for service quality, debugging, and security purposes; such telemetry does not constitute Feedback or Customer Content for the purposes of this Agreement."

Option B (Conservative / procurement-friendly):
- Customer ownership as above.
- Training prohibition: "Redwood shall not use Customer Content, Outputs, or Feedback to train models or improve model weights without a separate written agreement."
- Paid training path: optional addendum language to license back for a fee if customer later wants Redwood to use data for model retraining.

Risks/notes: Option A preserves us the ability to incorporate high-level, non-attributable improvements (bug fixes, safety rules) while Option B is cleaner for procurement but eliminates the ability to passively learn from aggregated signals. Telemetry carve is important operationally — we should be explicit about the definition and retention window.

I'll circulate the tracked changes shortly.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redlines_stellarmed.docx]
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Janet Liu <janet.liu@stellarmed.com>, Tim O'Neill <tim.oneill@venturelegal.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify output ownership & training consent in order form

Hi Janet / Tim — thanks for the clear mark-up. Attached are two concise redline options (see redlines_stellarmed.docx) that reflect Redwood's standard enterprise play: Option A (recommended) balances StellarMed ownership with a narrow feedback license and an explicit telemetry carve; Option B is a stricter procurement-friendly path that prohibits training without a paid addendum.

Summary:
- Outputs: StellarMed retains ownership of customer-generated Outputs in both options.
- Training: Option A limits Feedback to service improvement (no retraining without consent); Option B prohibits model training absent a separate agreement.
- Telemetry: We propose a defined telemetry carve limited to anonymized operational logs and a 90-day retention window for performance/debugging data.

Next steps:
1) Please tell us which option you prefer (A or B) and we'll incorporate into the MSA/order form.
2) If you pick Option B and anticipate wanting training later, we can include a templated paid training license schedule to avoid renegotiation.

If useful, Ben and I are available for a short call with Tim and your procurement/KYC team to finalize language today.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redlines_stellarmed.docx, SOC2_snapshot_2025.pdf]
